title: LSU Tries to Turn Chaos into College Football Antitrust Exemption
seoTitle: LSU Seeks Antitrust Exemption Amid College Football Chaos
subtitle: University President Uses Legal Dispute to Pressure Congress
excerpt: Amid eligibility controversies, LSU's president seeks legislative support for an antitrust exemption that could change transfer rules and more.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The debate over college football scores gained prominence in recent hours due to a legal controversy involving LSU. The dispute over the eligibility of former NFL players brought to light discussions about the need for an antitrust exemption for college sports.

Why LSU Is at the Center of the Discussion

LSU President Wade Rousse released a statement affirming respect for the judicial process and the court's decision. In the same message, he reaffirmed the intention to support the university's programs within the limits of the law and conference rules.

Objective of the Antitrust Exemption

Rousse emphasizes that the current instability in the college sports system justifies a continuous effort to obtain an exemption from Congress that would allow institutions to “partially dip into players' pockets” or limit athletes' freedom to change schools, similar to what happens with coaches.

Connection to the Brendan Sorsby Controversy

The controversy involving Brendan Sorsby and the dispute between LSU and the SEC regarding the return of former NFL players to college are cited as examples that highlight the need for a legislative framework, such as the Protect College Sports Act.

Impact on Roster Decisions

Rousse indicates that, given the possibility of adding two players before the season opener against Clemson, the university may choose not to proceed, evaluating the risk of harming its relationship with other SEC members.

Expectations for Congress

According to the statement, LSU will continue to work constructively with the SEC and the NCAA as the matter progresses, pointing out that college football “does not deserve this kind of ambiguity in eligibility standards.” The president reiterates that the situation illustrates the need for Congress to pass a version of the Protect College Sports Act.

With information from NBC Sports.
